newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sex is entertainment for poor in AIDS-hit SAfrica.
newsitem.headline: Sex is entertainment for poor in AIDS-hit SAfrica.

text.p: AIDS is surging in South Africa, where poor people end up having sex because they have no money to go to the movies or to the swimming pool, the country's health minister said on Wednesday.
"Sex is entertainment for the poor if you have nothing else to do when other people go to the cinema or to the pool, if your only relaxation is sex," Dlamini Zuma told reporters in Geneva.

UNAIDS, the United Nations coordinating agency for the AIDS epidemic, said 2.2 million people in South Africa, including an estimated 13 percent of its pregnant women, had the HIV virus which leads to AIDS.
Zuma said one of the worst-affected areas was the violence-hit Kwazulu-Natal province, where infection rates among pregnant women had reached 18 percent according to UNAIDS.
"When people face death today, the risk of death from AIDS in 10 years' time is a remote possibility for them," she said.
UNIADS said infection levels registered at South African health clinics were now higher than 20 percent compared with less than one percent in 1988.
"The country's health services are already starting to experience the impact of the epidemic," it said. "South Africa is just at the beginning of the curve of illness and death."
